title: SilverCreek Health — private deploy cheat sheet (onprem/VPC)
content:
Context:
- Customer: SilverCreek Health (regional hospital network, 12 sites). Wants private/private-managed Redwood instance inside their AWS account (VPC) with option for on-prem air-gapped later.
- Primary driver: PHI handling + auditability, SLA for ER triage assistant (clinical decision support).
- Contact: CISO: Lauren Meyers; IT infra: Tom Alvarez; product: Nina Park.

Meeting 2026-03-02 (30m) — quick sync notes:
- Lauren: must show proof of encryption-in-use/key control (HSM/KMS). No plaintext PHI leaves VPC.
- Tom: network team wants minimal public egress; prefer private endpoints + NAT controls.
- Nina: throughput target for initial pilot: ~200 inference req/s during peak with median req token length ~80 tokens; p95 latency target < 300ms for generation endpoints (critical).
- Derek (scoping): asked about fallback/GRACEFUL degradation — they expect model fallback to smaller quantized variant if capacity constrained.
- Riz from legal flagged logging retention: 7 years for certain audit logs, need export path to customer SIEM.

Requirements (explicit):
1) Private control plane in customer VPC (or customer-managed VPC peering) + support for later on-prem air-gapped bundle.
2) KMS/HSM integration: per-tenant keys, rotation policy, proof artifacts for compliance team.
3) No outbound PHI to hosted models — all inference on customer infra.
4) Observability: token-level cost/latency traces, per-route dashboards exported to their Grafana/Datadog, and audit logs exported to S3 bucket + SIEM collector.
5) Rollout policy: canary first to 2 sites, then ramp to all. Must support quick rollback to deterministic baseline model.
6) Throughput/latency: baseline throughput 200 rps, p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms (generations). Enable batching but preserve p95 target.
7) Model choices: start with 7B-like open model (quantized 4-bit) + fallback to a smaller 3B quantized variant. Evaluate 8k vs 32k context - prefer 8k for start.
8) Privacy pipeline: pre-send redaction + post-response PII scrubbers. Audit trail of redaction decisions.
9) Security: Mutual TLS for control plane, customer-managed certs, role separation for ops.

Operational gotchas / risk items (callout):
- NAT/egress: If some components require model catalog updates from Redwood servers, need offline sync path or CARP (customer accept remote fetch) — avoid any PHI in those calls.
- KMS latency: HSM signing/calls on hot path could add 40–80ms; benchmark with HSM sim before commit. Consider token encryption key caching with short TTL.
- KV cache sizing: with many short sessions, KV hot cache memory footprint could spike. Need to size GPU RAM + provision swap/eviction strategy.
- Autoscale warmup: cold-starts to new machines add >1s in worst case — must pre-warm based on scheduled shifts (ER peaks).
- Quantized accuracy vs hallucination: smaller quantized variants may regress on clinical phrasing—need eval set.
- Audit log volume: 200 rps * token traces => LOTS of telemetry. Confirm retention/cost model for S3 + SIEM.
- On-prem network ops: firewall rules for NTP, CRL/OCSP for certs; air-gapped mode must include a signed bundle of models + kernels.

Suggested initial architecture (sketch):
- Control plane: customer VPC hosted control plane components (control-plane API + console) behind ALB with mTLS.
- Inference plane: dedicated GPU pool (ec2-g5/spot-protected?) within same VPC, autoscaler in private subnets.
- KMS: customer-managed AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys; use short-lived local DEKs cached per serving node.
- Logging: Fluentd -> secure s3 bucket (encrypted) + push to their SIEM.
- Model storage: EFS/put-model-cache in private subnet or preloaded on-instance images.

Evaluation plan (to mitigate hallucination / regressions):
- Build a 200–400 prompt evaluation set from their real-sanitized triage logs (legal to approve).
- Track MRR/ROUGE-like metrics + specific clinical safety recalls.
- Set a quality threshold for rollouts: delta in helpfulness < 2% and false-positive hallucination < 0.5%.

Action items (owner — due):
- Riley: draft SOW bullet list + architecture sketch for legal review (due 2026-03-17).
- Maya: spin up HSM latency micro-bench with simulated traffic (JIRA STH-452) and attach numbers (due 2026-03-12).
- Derek: prototype small onprem bundle flow (signed model bundle + installer) and open PR (github PR link above) (due 2026-03-21).
- Tom (customer): confirm retention policy + SIEM endpoint and provide sample log format (due 2026-03-14).
- Priya: prepare eval prompt set redaction template and process doc for compliance (due 2026-03-18).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can legal accept short-term telemetry to Redwood for debugging under strict NDA (helps root-cause for perf issues)?
- Do they require FIPS-140-2 validation for all crypto paths or only for keys at rest? Need exact spec from Lauren.
- Bandwidth constraints: do we need to support multi-region DR? If yes, how to replicate model artifacts safely?

Notes-to-self (quick):
- When proposing pricing, call out overhead for long audit-retention + high telemetry.
- For pilot, recommend reserved capacity with dedicated pre-warmed nodes for ER windows.
- Keep fallback policy explicit: model A (quant4 7B) -> model B (quant4 3B) -> degraded mode (rate-limited prompts + canned response template).

Meeting cadence proposal:
- Weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks (Riley + Tom + Maya) + biweekly tech deep-dive with infra + security.

Misc tiny references / tickets:
- JIRA STH-452: HSM perf microbench (owner: Maya).
- JIRA STH-459: Audit log retention + SIEM export (owner: Tom).
- GH: infra-provision PR#128 (Derek) — installer skeleton.

End of scratchpad.
